sections.english: We must take into our reckoning not only that life is expended day by day and the remaining balance diminishes, but also this further consideration: if we live longer, there is no guarantee that our mind will remain sufficient for the understanding of fact and for the theory which enables an expertise in things divine and human. It is true that dementia can set in, and then the functions of breath, nutrition, fancy, impulse, and so on will not fail. But the ability to make use of ourselves, to fill out the measure of our duties, to analyse appearances, to make the crucial decision whether it is time to take our leave — all this and other such processes which depend entirely on the exercised reason, is already extinguished. So we must press on, not simply because we move closer to death all the time, but because our comprehension of the world and our ability to pay proper attention will fade before us.
sections.chinese: 吾辈计虑之中，不仅当知生命日复一日耗减、余存日益萎缩，更当思及此节：纵使寿数稍延，心智是否仍足以理解事实、仍足以掌握通晓神人之事的理论，实无保证。痴愚确然可能降临，届时呼吸、营养、想象、冲动等诸般功能亦未必失却。然运用自身之力、践行职分之能、分析表象之明、作此关键决断——是否当辞世而去——凡此种种及其他一应全然依赖训练有素之理性的过程，已然熄灭矣。故吾辈当亟亟前行，非仅因时时趋近死亡，更因吾辈对世界之理解与专注于事之能力，将先于吾人而消逝。

sections.english: We should also attend to things like these, observing that even the incidental effects of the processes of Nature have their own charm and attraction. Take the baking of bread. The loaf splits open here and there, and these cracks, though in a sense escaping the design of the baker, have their own charm and a lively stimulus to appetite. Figs, again, split open when fully ripe: in the olives left on the tree, the very proximity of decay lends a particular beauty to the fruit. So too the bending heads of corn, the lion's frown, the foam at the boar's mouth, and many other things — far from beautiful in isolation, yet the consequence of some other process beautifies them and gives them attraction. So any man with a feeling and deeper insight for the workings of the Whole will find some pleasure in almost every aspect of their disposition, including the incidental consequences.
sections.chinese: 吾辈亦当留意如此等事，察见即便是自然运化之附带效果，亦有其独有之韵味与引力。以烤制面包为例，面包坯体处处开裂，而这些罅隙虽在某种意义上逸出焙烤者之设计，却自有其韵致，更激人食欲。又如无花果，完全成熟之际自然裂开；橄榄之留在树上者，正因其近乎腐烂而赋予果实一种独特之美。弯垂之麦穗、雄狮之蹙额、野猪嘴边之唾沫，以及其他种种——单独观之远非美丽，然作为其他过程之后果，反增其美且赋予其魅力。故人若对宇宙整体之运作有情致与慧眼，在几乎每一方面之配置中——包括那些附带之后果——均能获得某种愉悦。

sections.english: Hippocrates cured many diseases then died of disease himself. The Chaldean astrologers foretold the deaths of many people, then their own fated day claimed them. Alexander, Pompey, Julius Caesar annihilated whole cities time and again, slaughtering tens of thousands of cavalry and infantry in pitched battle, then their own day came. Heraclitus speculated long on the conflagration of the universe, then died swollen with water and caked with cow-dung. Vermin killed Democritus; another sort of vermin killed Socrates. What of it? You embarked, you set sail, you made landfall. Step ashore then. If that means a new life, there is no want of gods even in that other world. But if it is a state of blank unconsciousness, then you will cease to be subject to pain and pleasure and servitude to the flesh — this vessel so much baser than that which is its slave. The one is mind and divinity, the other clay and putrefying blood.
sections.chinese: 希波克拉底治愈无数疾病，而后自身死于疾病。迦勒底占星家预卜众多人等的死亡，而后他们自己命定之日也将他们收去。亚历山大、庞培、尤利乌斯·凯撒一次又一次夷平整座城池，在列阵之战中屠戮成千上万之骑兵与步兵，而后他们自己也等来了那一天。赫拉克利特长久沉思宇宙之大火，而后浑身水胀、满涂牛粪而死。虱虫杀死了德谟克利特；另一种虱虫杀死了苏格拉底。这又如何？你登船起航，扬帆而行，抵达彼岸。那便上岸吧。若彼处是新生，彼一世界中亦不匮乏诸神。但若只是空白无觉之境，则你将不再受制于苦乐，不再受役于肉体——此器皿远较为其奴者更为卑下。一者为心与神，一者为泥土与腐血。

sections.english: Do not waste the remaining part of your life in thoughts about other people, when you are not thinking with reference to some aspect of the common good. Why deprive yourself of the time for some other task? I mean, thinking about what so-and-so is doing, and why, what he is saying, what he is plotting, and all the other lines of thought which make you stray from the close watch on your own directing mind. We must then avoid in the chain of our thoughts all that is random and aimless: still more important is the avoidance of meddlesome and malicious thought. We should habituate ourselves to think only of those things about which, if anyone were suddenly to ask: 'What are you thinking of now?', you could at once freely reply: 'This' or 'That.' Then it would be immediately plain from the answer that all is simplicity and kindness — the thought of a social being who has no regard for the seductions of pleasure or of self-indulgence, nor for rivalry, malice, suspicion, or anything else which you would blush to admit you had in mind.
sections.chinese: 莫将余生虚掷于思虑他人之事——若你所思并非涉及公共福祉之某一方面。为何剥夺自己从事他务之时日？我意所指，乃是：思量某人正在做何事、为何而做、所言何语、所图何谋，以及一切使你疏于严密看守自己主导心灵之思绪。故吾辈须在思绪之链条中避开一切漫无目的与随机漂移之物；更要紧者，须避干涉与恶意之思。当养成为此习惯：仅思虑此等事——若有人猝然发问：「你此刻所思何事？」，你能即刻坦然答曰：「某事某物」。如此，从答案中当即显明一切皆质朴而善好——此乃一个社会性存在者之思绪，彼不顾及逸乐或放纵之引诱，亦不顾及争强、恶意、猜忌，或任何使你羞于承认存于心中之事物。

sections.english: You should take no action unwillingly, selfishly, uncritically, or with conflicting motives. Do not dress up your thoughts in smart finery: do not be a gabbler or a meddler. Further, let the god that is within you be the guardian of a real man, a man of ripe years, a statesman, a Roman, a ruler: one who has taken his post, waiting for the signal of his release from life, ready for his departure, needing no oath of others nor any witness to his readiness. And a happy countenance in yourself, with no need of external help or the peace given by others. You need to stand straight, not straightened by others.
sections.chinese: 凡所行动，不当心存不愿、自私自利、不加审察，或动机彼此冲突。勿以花巧之装束文饰你的思想；勿为喋喋不休者或好管闲事者。更有进者，令你心中之神明守护一个真正之人——一个年岁成熟之人，一个政治家，一个罗马人，一个统治者：他已就任其岗位，等候被释放出生之信号，准备好启程，不赖他人之誓言或证词以明其就绪。你当自有怡然之色，不假外助，亦无需他人所给之平静。你需自行直立，而非被人扶正。

sections.english: If you discover in human life something better than justice, truth, self-control, courage — in short, something better than the self-sufficiency of your own mind which keeps you acting in accord with true reason and your fate in whatever is assigned to you without your own choice: if, I say, you can see something better than this, then turn to it with all your heart and enjoy this prime good you have found. But if nothing is shown to be better than the very god that is seated in you, which has brought all your own impulses under its control, which scrutinizes your thoughts, which (in the words of Socrates) has withdrawn itself from all prompting of the senses, which holds itself answerable to the gods and devotes its care to humankind — if you find all else paltry and trivial by comparison with this, give no room to anything else. Once diverted and inclined that way, you will no longer have the ability to honour without reservation that other good, which is your own proper good.
sections.chinese: 若你在人生中发现了优于正义、真理、自制、勇气之物——简言之，优于你那自足之心灵之物，此心灵使你依据真实理性而行动，并接纳命运分配于你而非你自择之一切——若你发现胜于此者，便倾全心以赴之，享受你所觅得的此一至善。然而，若无一物显示优于那高居你内之神明——此神明已统驭你所有之冲动，细察你之思想，如苏格拉底所言已从一切感官驱使中撤回自身，自负其对诸神之责，而将关切倾注于人类——若你发觉与此相较，其他一切皆微不足道、琐屑不堪，则当不容他物有一席之地。一旦偏转而倾向于彼方，你便再无能力毫无保留地尊崇那别一善者——那属于你自己的、本己之善。

sections.english: Never regard as a benefit to yourself anything which will force you at some point to break your faith, to leave integrity behind, to hate, suspect, or curse another, to dissemble, to covet anything needing walls and curtains.
sections.chinese: 凡迫使你在某一刻背弃信义、抛弃正直、憎恨、猜忌或咒骂他人、伪饰假装、贪求需用墙帷遮掩之物的东西，永勿视之为于己有益。

sections.english: In the mind of one who is chastened and cleansed you will find no suppuration, no simmering ulcer, no sore festering under the skin. Fate does not catch him with his life unfulfilled, as one might speak of an actor leaving the stage before his part is finished and the play ended. Moreover there is nothing servile or pretentious, no dependency on others or severance from them, no sense of responsibility, no sense of guilt.
sections.chinese: 在一个经锤炼而净化之人的心灵中，你找不到化脓之处、找不到慢火灼烧的溃疡，也找不到皮下溃烂的肿疮。命运不会将其生之未满而掳走，犹如人言一伶人未演完戏份之前便离开舞台。此外，其中既无奴颜婢膝，亦无矫揉造作，既无依赖他人，亦无与人疏隔，既无牵挂，亦无罪咎。

sections.english: Revere your power of judgement. All rests on this to make sure that your directing mind no longer entertains any judgement which fails to agree with the nature or the constitution of a rational being. This guarantees deliberate thought, affinity with other men, and obedience to the gods.
sections.chinese: 敬汝判断之能。一切皆系于此：确保你那主导之心灵不再容纳任何与理性存在者之本性或构造不相合的判断。此即是审慎之思、与人之亲近、以及对诸神之服从的保证。

sections.english: So discard all else and secure these few things only. Remind yourself too that each of us lives only in the present moment, a mere fragment of time: the rest is life past or uncertain future. Sure, life is a small thing, and small the cranny of the earth in which we live it: and small too even the longest fame thereafter, which itself is a succession of puny mortals, who will very soon be dead, with no knowledge of themselves, let alone people long since dead and buried.
sections.chinese: 故当抛弃其余一切，仅守护此寥寥数事。亦当自省：吾辈每人仅活在此一当下此刻，不过时间之一微片耳：其余或为已逝之生命，或为未定之将来。固然，生命是渺小之物，吾人赖以生存之地之罅隙亦渺小：甚至死后最长之名声亦然渺小——此名不过是递相传承之渺小凡人所传，彼等亦将很快死去，于己身尚且无知，遑论早已故去掩埋之人。

sections.english: One addition to the precepts already mentioned. Always make a definition or sketch of what presents itself to your mind, so you can see it stripped bare to its essential nature and identify it clearly, in its entirety, and tell yourself its proper name, and the names of the elements from which it was compounded and into which it will be dissolved. Nothing so elevates the mind as the ability to examine methodically and truly every object presented to you in life, and always to look at things so as to see at the same time what kind of universe this is, what part it plays in that universe, what value it has in relation to the Whole and what value to man as a citizen of that highest city of which all other cities are like households.
sections.chinese: 于上述诸训之外，复加一条。凡有事物呈现于你心中，便为之作一定义或草图，如此你能见其赤裸剥离至其本质真性，清晰辨明其全貌，并告己以其确切之名，以及构成与终将分解之元素的名目。没有什么比此更提撕心灵：能以方法逐一真实审视生命中所呈现之每一对象，并恒常如此看待事物——同时洞见此为何等之宇宙、此物在此宇宙中扮演何等角色，与整体相对有何价值，与人——作为那最高之城邦的公民，其他一切城邦不过是此城邦之家族——相对又有何价值。

sections.english: If you set yourself to your present task along the path of true reason, with all determination, vigour, and good will: if you admit no distraction, but keep your own divinity pure and standing strong, as if you must now give it back; if you engage with your task, expecting nothing and avoiding nothing, but content with each present action taken in accordance with nature and with heroic truth in all that you say and speak — then you will live a good life. And there is no one who can prevent this.
sections.chinese: 若你遵循真正理性之道路，以全部决心、精力与善意，专注于你当下之任务；若你不容任何纷扰，保持你自身之神性纯净而屹立强劲，仿佛此刻便须归还于彼；若你投入其事，无所期待亦无所回避，而满足于每一当下依自然而采取之行动，并于所说所言中持守英雄般之真诚——你便将善度此生。且无人能阻挡你如此。

sections.english: Just as doctors always have their instruments and knives at hand for any emergency treatment, so you should have your doctrines ready for the recognition of the divine and the human, and the performance of even your smallest action in the consciousness of the bond which unites the two.
sections.chinese: 正如医者随时备有其器械与刀具于手边以应紧急治疗，你亦当备好你的教义——用以辨识神圣与人事，且令你之行止，即便最为琐屑之行动，也均在有意识于联结二者之纽带中进行。

sections.english: No more wandering. You are not likely to read your own jottings, your histories of the ancient Greeks and Romans, your extracts from their literature laid up for your old age. Hurry then to the end, abandon idle hopes, and come to your own rescue, if you have any care for yourself, while the opportunity is still yours.
sections.chinese: 不要再游荡。你未必会去读你自己那些劄记、那些古希腊罗马史乘、那些为晚年而备辑之文献钞录。那便疾速奔赴终点吧，舍弃虚空之盼，自救于沉溺——若你对自己尚有丝毫顾念，趁机缘尚在手中。

sections.english: They do not know all the meanings of theft, of sowing, of buying, of keeping at rest, of seeing what needs to be done — this is not for the eye, but for a different sort of vision.
sections.chinese: 彼等不知盗窃之诸义，不知播种之诸义，不知买卖之诸义，不知静守之诸义，不知察见本当为之事——此非肉眼所能见，而需另一种观照。

sections.english: Body, soul, mind. To the body belong sense perceptions, to the soul impulses, to the mind judgements. The receipt of sense impressions is shared with cattle; response to the puppet-strings of impulse is shared with wild beasts, with catamites, with a Phalaris or a Nero; the guide of the mind to its proper objects is shared with those who deny the gods, with those who betray their own country, with those who do anything behind locked doors. So if all else is held in common with the categories mentioned above, it follows that the defining characteristic of the good person is to love and embrace whatever happens to him along his thread of fate; and not to pollute the divinity which is seated within his heart or trouble it with a welter of confused ideas, but to preserve its favour, following god in orderly manner, uttering nothing contrary to truth, doing nothing contrary to justice. And if all people mistrust him, or oppose him, or set upon him, he cannot be shaken. Nevertheless he meets his death with serenity: neither crushed by this nor carried away by his gift, but of himself a willing and unreluctant departure.
sections.chinese: 身体、魂、心灵。感官知觉属于身体，冲动属于魂，判断属于心灵。接受感官印象，与牲畜所共有；对冲动之提线木偶般回应，与野兽、娈童、法拉里斯或尼禄之辈所共有；以心灵引导至恰当之对象，与否神者、叛国者、以及一切在锁闭之门后为非作歹者所共有。故，若其他一切皆与上述诸类所共有，则善人之界定特征便是：爱且拥抱沿其命运之线落到他身上的一切遭遇；且不以混乱芜杂之念污染安座其内心之神性，亦不以此搅扰之，而是有序列地追随神明，保守其恩眷，口不出违背真理之言，事不有违正义之行。纵使众人不信任他、反对他、围攻他，他亦岿然不动。纵是如此，他坦然赴死：既不被死亡所摧垮，亦不为其禀赋所裹挟飘然，而乃出于自己意愿、无所勉强地辞行。
